summary: 人体嗅觉的灵敏度长期被低估。实验发现，人能区分很细微的气味差异，气味还可能影响清洁行为、认知判断和记忆的情绪强度，尤其容易勾起童年回忆。
logic: 回顾人类嗅觉较差的旧观点
检测与辨别气味的实验

paragraphs.brief: 人类嗅觉被低估的影响
sentences: Dogs’ noses are renowned for sensitivity to smells, while human noses are thought to be poor by comparison, yet that might be a misconception.
狗的嗅觉灵敏是出了名的，人们常以为人鼻相形见绌，但这可能是误解。
According to recent studies, our noses are in fact acutely sensitive instruments that guide our everyday lives to a surprising extent.
最近的研究表明，人的鼻子其实极其灵敏，对日常生活的影响大得出人意料。
Subtle smells can change your mood, behaviour and the choices you make, often without you realising it.
微弱的气味可以在你浑然不觉时改变你的心情、行为和选择。
Our own odours, meanwhile, indicate emotional states such as fear or sadness to those around us.
与此同时，我们自身的气味也会向旁人传递恐惧或悲伤等情绪。
The big mystery is why we aren’t more aware of our nasal activity.
最大的谜团在于，为什么我们这么少留意鼻子在做什么。
Noses have certainly never been at the forefront of sensory research, and were pushed aside until recently in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing.
嗅觉一向不是感官研究的重点，直到最近仍被看似更重要的视觉和听觉挤在一旁。

‘There has been a lot of prejudice that people are not that influenced by olfactory stimuli, especially compared to other mammals,’ says Lilianne Mujica-Parodi, who studies the neurobiology of human stress at Stony Brook University in New York, in the United States.
在美国纽约州立大学石溪分校研究人类应激反应的神经生物学家莉莉安·穆希卡-帕罗迪说：「人们有种根深蒂固的成见，以为人类受嗅觉刺激的影响很小，尤其是跟其他哺乳动物相比。」
paragraphs.gist: 人常以为自己的鼻子远不如狗，研究却发现微弱的气味能悄悄左右选择，人体发出的气味还会向旁人传递情绪。

paragraphs.brief: 布罗卡按嗅觉依赖程度分类
sentences: One of the first people to assert the relative unimportance of human smelling was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist.
十九世纪颇有影响的解剖学家皮埃尔·保罗·布罗卡，是最早主张嗅觉对人类没那么重要的学者之一。

After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while we, along with other primates and the marine mammals, are microsmatic – we have small olfactory organs that we only rely on to a small extent.
他比较了不同动物脑中负责嗅觉的区域所占的比例，把哺乳动物分为两大类：狗等嗅觉发达的动物主要靠敏锐的嗅觉感知世界；人类、其他灵长类和海洋哺乳动物则嗅觉器官较小，对它依赖也较少。
That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies which found that the majority of mammals have genes coding for about 1000 different types of smell receptor.
后来的研究发现，多数哺乳动物具有可编码约一千种嗅觉受体的基因，这似乎符合他的看法。
Most of these genes aren’t expressed in humans, giving our noses just 400 different types of receptor.
这些基因大多不在人类体内表达，因此人鼻只有约四百种嗅觉受体。
paragraphs.gist: 布罗卡依据脑中嗅觉区域的占比，把人类归入较少依赖嗅觉的一类；后来发现人鼻的受体种类较少，似乎支持他的观点。

paragraphs.brief: 脑区连接与微量气味检测
sentences: Yet these findings may have been misleading.
然而，这些调查结果可能误导了人们。
Brain scans now show that more of the brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca’s anatomical studies suggested.
如今的脑部扫描显示，参与处理气味的脑区比布罗卡的解剖研究所估计的更广。

And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, Charles Greer at Yale University in the United States has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals.
尽管人类的受体种类可能比其他哺乳动物少，耶鲁大学的查尔斯·格雷尔却发现，人鼻和大脑之间的联系异常丰富，每组受体连接的神经区域都远多于其他动物。
That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.
这应当赋予我们很强的气味处理能力。
Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested.
研究者认真检验后发现，人的嗅觉远比通常认为的灵敏。
One study, for example, found that we can detect certain chemicals diluted in water to less than one part per billion.
例如，一项研究发现，某些化学物质在水中稀释到浓度不足十亿分之一时，人仍能闻出来。
That means that a person can detect just a few drops of a strong smell like ethyl mercaptan in an Olympic-sized pool.
这相当于在一个奥运会标准泳池里只滴入几滴乙硫醇之类气味浓烈的物质，人也能察觉。
paragraphs.gist: 脑部扫描显示人类用于处理气味的脑区比过去以为的广，每组受体连接的区域也多，人甚至能察觉水中浓度低于十亿分之一的某些物质。

paragraphs.brief: 分辨相似气味及其情绪联系
sentences: ‘We are also exceptionally gifted at telling smells apart, even in the case of two molecules whose only difference is that their structures are mirror images of one another.
「我们也特别善于区分气味，哪怕两种分子的结构唯一的差别是彼此互为镜像。
That is fantastic sensitivity,’ says George Dodd, a perfumer and researcher at the olfaction group of the University of Warwick, in the United Kingdom.
这样的灵敏度实在惊人。」英国华威大学嗅觉研究小组的调香师兼研究员乔治·多德说。
What’s more, it’s becoming clear that the brain’s olfactory centres are intimately linked to its limbic system, which is involved in emotion, fear and memory.
此外，越来越多证据表明，大脑的嗅觉中枢与参与处理情绪、恐惧和记忆的边缘系统紧密相连。
That suggests a link between smell and the way we think.
这提示嗅觉可能与思考方式有关。
paragraphs.gist: 即便两个分子的结构仅互为镜像，人也能辨别气味；嗅觉中枢与处理情绪、恐惧和记忆的边缘系统还紧密相连。

paragraphs.brief: 气味改变夜店和宿舍中的行为
sentences: The power of smell will be no news to estate agents, who often advocate the smell of baking bread or brewing coffee to promote the sale of a house.
房产经纪人早已熟悉气味的作用，他们常建议借烤面包或煮咖啡的香味促进房屋销售。
But there are more subtle and surprising effects too.
但也有更微妙和令人惊讶的效果。

When Hendrik Schifferstein and colleagues, from Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, pumped the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint into a nightclub, the revellers danced more, rated their night as more enjoyable, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.
荷兰代尔夫特理工大学的研究者把橙子、海水或薄荷的气味送入夜店，结果客人跳舞更多，觉得当晚更愉快，甚至认为音乐比没有添加气味时更好听。

Meanwhile, Rob Holland, of the University of Utrecht in the Netherlands, found that the hint of aroma wafting out of a hidden bucket of citrus-scented cleaner was enough to persuade students in a hostel to clean up after themselves.
荷兰乌得勒支大学的罗布·霍兰发现，只要把一桶柑橘味清洁剂藏起来，让香气微微飘出，就能促使住在宿舍的学生主动收拾自己弄乱的地方。
paragraphs.gist: 气味能在不知不觉中改变行为：夜店添香让顾客跳舞更多，宿舍里淡淡的柑橘清洁剂气味也能促使学生主动收拾。

paragraphs.brief: 陌生气味干扰决策表现
sentences: Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills.
其他研究还发现，气味可以影响认知能力。

A study by William Overman and colleagues at the University of North Carolina in the United States found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal.
美国北卡罗来纳大学的威廉·奥弗曼及其同事发现，男性在决策测试时若闻到陌生气味，无论好闻还是难闻，表现都明显不如平常。
The researchers conclude the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
研究人员认为，气味刺激了与情绪有关的脑区，使参与者的判断更多受情绪支配，较少依靠理性。
paragraphs.gist: 男性在决策测试中闻到陌生气味时表现明显变差，研究者认为无论气味好坏，它都可能调动情绪，使判断较少依靠理性。

paragraphs.brief: 气味唤起的记忆更富情感
sentences: Smells are especially good memory evokers, but it is actually a myth that odours trigger more detailed memories than other stimuli.
气味特别容易勾起回忆，但说气味比其他刺激唤起更多细节，其实是个误区。
‘The memory is not more accurate and you don’t remember more details,’ says Yaara Yeshurun at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, ‘but it is unique in that it is more emotional.’
以色列魏茨曼科学研究所的雅拉·耶舒伦说：「回忆并非更准确，你也不会记起更多细节；它的特殊之处在于情感更强烈。」
This isn’t surprising when you consider that there are certain brain areas dedicated to both emotion and olfaction, such as the amygdala, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory.
这个结果并不奇怪。有些脑区同时处理情绪和嗅觉，例如杏仁核，而情绪与记忆的联系又十分紧密。
In 2009, Yeshurun found that the link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is unpleasant rather than pleasant.
2009 年，耶舒伦发现，难闻的气味比好闻的气味更容易与回忆形成牢固的联结。

She also discovered that the very first time we attach a smell to an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any subsequent encounter with the smell or object, laying down stronger foundations for the memory.
她还发现，初次将气味与物体联系起来时，大脑的反应远强于后来再次遇到该气味或物体时，因而记忆的根基更深。
That doesn’t happen with any other sense.
其他感官都没有表现出这种现象。
Since those first encounters with a smell would have happened at a young age, this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.
初次接触某种气味往往是在小时候，这解释了为什么气味常常能让我们一下子回到童年。
paragraphs.gist: 气味唤起的回忆更富情感，未必更精确；难闻的气味和初次形成的气味联结格外牢固，也解释了熟悉的气味为何常让人想起童年。

items.en: a finding that humans can distinguish between two extremely similar substances
items.zh: 发现人类可以区分两种极为相似的物质
items.why: “tell…apart (分辨)”=distinguish。“two molecules…mirror images”=“两种极其相似的物质”。其他段未谈“镜像分子” 的对比，故。

items.en: a categorisation of species according to their sensitivity to smell
items.zh: 按对气味的敏感程度给物种分类
items.why: B段介绍按嗅觉有关脑区的比例，把哺乳动物划为嗅觉强、弱两大类。

items.en: an instance where smell negatively affected people’s ability to make choices
items.zh: 气味妨碍人们作出选择的实例
items.why: “performed worse”=能力受负面影响。主题是“决策任务 (choices/decision-making)”。其他段虽谈气味影响，但未涉及“变差/负面”。

items.en: a study that proved humans could perceive a tiny quantity of a substance
items.zh: 一项证明人类能感觉到微量物质的研究
items.why: 研究发现，即使某些化学物质稀释到不足十亿分之一，人仍能察觉，符合题干的极微量。

items.en: an observation that studies of the sense of smell have been undervalued
items.zh: 指出嗅觉研究长期未获应有重视
items.why: A段说嗅觉长期没有成为感官研究的重点，逊于视觉等感官受到的关注。

items.en: an example of using smell to prompt people to buy something
items.zh: 一个用气味来吸引人们买东西的例子
items.why: “prompt people to buy” =~ “promote the sale’。E段还举夜店与清洁例，但“购买/交易” 对应卖房情境。

items.en: A faint smell could motivate people to do household chores
items.zh: 淡淡的气味可能促使人主动做家务。

items.en: Humans are better equipped to interpret smell than other species are
items.zh: 人类辨读气味的能力比其他物种更强。

items.en: Smell is associated with feelings, rather than the logical part of the brain
items.zh: 气味与情绪有关，跟大脑中负责逻辑思考的部分关系较小。

items.en: Humans do not require a sophisticated ability to smell
items.zh: 人类不需要特别灵敏的嗅觉。

items.en: The ________ is a part of the brain that deals with feelings and smell.
items.zh: 大脑中负责处理情绪和气味的部位是________。
items.why: 题干限定“一词”。,专名小写作答。

items.en: ________ smells create especially powerful associations with memories.
items.zh: ________的气味尤其容易与记忆形成牢固的联系。
items.why: 比较级触发词“rather than pleasant” 提示答案取“unpleasant”。

items.en: Of all the senses, smell has the capacity to prompt memories of ________.
items.zh: 在所有感官中，嗅觉能够唤起有关________的记忆。
items.why: 填“childhood”(不可填“our childhood memories”,因题干已含“memories of…” 结构)。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: “prompt people to buy” =~ “promote the sale’。E段还举夜店与清洁例，但“购买/交易” 对应卖房情境。
比较级触发词“rather than pleasant” 提示答案取“unpleasant”。
clauses: Dogs’ noses are renowned for sensitivity to smells, …, yet that might be a misconception.
连接词 while 引出“while human noses are thought to be poor by comparison”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
‘There has been a lot of prejudice that people are not that influenced by olfactory stimuli, especially compared to other mammals,’ says Lilianne Mujica-Parodi, …, in the United States.
“who studies the neurobiology of human stress at Stony Brook University in New York”修饰前面的 Parodi。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 Parodi，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Research shows that our olfactory sense is more influential than we realise
研究表明，嗅觉对我们的影响比自己意识到的更大。
